response.passage: Mobile phones are a common part of our lives, but many myths surround them. One common concern is about mobile towers. Mobile towers use radio waves to transmit signals, which are a form of non-ionising radiation. Unlike X-rays, these waves lack the energy to damage human cells or cause illness. Another myth is that phones emit the same amount of radiation constantly. In reality, your phone automatically adjusts its power output based on the signal strength; it uses less power when the signal is strong and more when the signal is weak. People also worry about their phone getting warm. A phone feels warm because of the energy used by the processor or battery during operation, not because it is emitting dangerous radiation. Furthermore, radio waves are electromagnetic waves, not sound waves, so they travel perfectly well through the vacuum of space without needing air. Finally, regarding eye health, while staring at a screen for a long time can cause temporary eye strain, it does not cause permanent blindness. To keep your eyes healthy, follow the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds, rather than taking one long break after hours of use.
response.summary: Mobile phones use safe, non-ionising radio waves that do not cause illness or radiation buildup. Phones adjust their power output based on signal strength, and screen use causes temporary strain rather than permanent damage.
